steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: You came.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Of course I did. That's what you do when the Nings invite you.

steps.name: Xingzhu
steps.text: ...I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hide anything from you. I just... don't really think it's something I should bring up for no reason...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Nothing to apologize for. You've got your troubles. I'm not the kind to give you the stink eye just for being blue-blooded.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Sooo, what do I call you, lady of House Ning?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: My name is... Ning Yin.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I'm... not actually part of House Ning. I was adopted by Grandfather as a child.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: He always introduced me as a distant relative of the Nings, but I've never met any 'relative' who actually shares blood with me.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Do you remember what I told you before?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Look, I'm pretty bad at comforting people...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: No, it's okay. Grandfather's very nice to me, and my background has never caused me any trouble at all... everyone treats me very well.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Your grandpa would be... Ning Shu? Ex-Minister of Rites?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Perfect, I—

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I know... I know.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It's getting chilly. Don't just stand out there, let's go inside and talk. Okay?

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Sure, I guess.
The corridor meanders on, through a rock garden and a bamboo thicket, then between the two halves of a lotus pond.

A cool breeze brushes through; the autumn waters softly ripple, and in them Blaze's reflection follows behind Ning Yin's as they pace across the bridge. The two pass through a deserted room, packed-up belongings and dead leaves strewn everywhere.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: The courtyard is messy, I know. Not presentable to guests, at the very least. I apologize.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: The whole family's moving out of here soon. Grandfather can't take Baizao's dry climate in his old age. We're planning to move back to the old place in Jiangnan.
Though Ning Yin's pace is glacial, she can only hurry up once she notices her friend in no mood to appreciate the scenery.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Up ahead. We're almost there.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Take a seat. I'll fetch some tea and refreshments from the kitchen. Our house cooks are all on leave, so I can't serve you much more than some cold sides—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: No need to bother. I can't stick around long.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: ...Are things that urgent?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Well, alright...
Ning softly closes the door. The chirps of fowl outside fade. The room grows heavier with silence.

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Alright. Tell me why you invited me here.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I'm sorry... I was going to look for you yesterday, actually, after the fire at Ding Feng Lou.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But I overheard your conversation with the Deputy Minister of Judicial Review Office and Chef Mo...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: And?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Blaze, I... might have met your father before.
When I was fifteen years old, I remember we had a visitor.
Grandfather was always busy with work. His apprentices and coworkers were coming and going in the estate. None of my business, by and large.
But slowly, I realized an extra person had moved in, wearing blue low-ranking mandarin's robes. Every time I saw him, he was alone, as if other people just weren't his concern.
At first, I didn't really pay attention. It was later that year, on my birthday, when...
Like every other year, Grandfather would hold this great big birthday dinner for me.
With lights and banners strung up everywhere, and friends and family all around... not that I knew more than a handful of them.
They were chatting the day away, and about what, I had no clue. So eventually I sneaked out of the dinner, and nobody noticed when I did.
I wandered around the courtyard for ages, bored out of my mind, then scampered into Grandfather's study on a whim.
It was in there where I saw the man again.
I remember I saw him stuffing his pocket with letter papers and brushes. When he noticed me, his face was stretched with nervousness, and he pulled the brush and paper back out again in a rush.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Are you...

steps.name: Agitated Man
steps.text: It's not what it looks like!

steps.name: Agitated Man
steps.text: I... needed to finish copying some letters, so I was going to take them home. The High Minister is sending these to very important mandarins, so I was just worried if the paper wasn't good enough...

steps.name: Agitated Man
steps.text: I just...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It's okay, it's just brushes and paper. You're welcome to make use of it, Sir.

steps.name: Agitated Man
steps.text: Thank you, little lady.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Um, what's your name...?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: My name is... Gu Quan. I'm a transcriber for your estate. I copy and file the estate correspondence.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I'm Ning Yin...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Miss Ning... Of course, I know you.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Then now we know each other.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Sir, I want to read in here for a bit. I won't interrupt you while you work. Is that okay?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: O—Of course...! Feel free, Miss Ning.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm-hm.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Miss Ning... are you into these history books?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm-hm. Grandfather always says one should view history as a mirror. We must use it to study our ancestors' wisdom and character, and learn from their teachings.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But I think reading's just fun. It's like all these amazing people recorded in the texts are coming to life before me, and they're all my friends.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I think someday, it might be nice to join the Imperial Historical Cabinet as a historian myself.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: You've got quite a unique outlook, Miss Ning...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: If you're interested in following in the High Minister's family footsteps, I'm sure you'd do well.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: You think Grandfather's really cool too, then?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: ...Of course. Minister Ning's been helming the Ministry of Rites for decades. He has plenty of deeds to his name. He's the mandarin everyone loves.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm-hm... everyone in this family is so cool.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: My uncle and aunt are always away from Baizao, traveling all over the country. I hear Yan couldn't have set up the meteorological and earthquake systems it has today without them.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: And Ciqiu, my little sister, she's even cooler.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: She's two years younger than me, but at the last Baizao Academy study camp, all the professors from the college of foreign affairs were praising her! Everyone was teasing her by calling her 'Little Miss Minister'!

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: All the people in my family are going to leave their names in the history books.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I love them and respect them a lot. I want to record who they are, and everything they do... but I could never become like them.

spans.text: I love them and respect them a lot. I want to record who they are, and everything they do... but I could never

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Compared to them, I'm just... normal.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: You know, that reminds me of something my master once said to me.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: 'As history has ebbed and flowed, the floods and tides are recorded, yet most are streams that simply trickle on by... But without the babbling brook, how would the waves arise?'

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: The waves and brooks don't care about who's greater, or who's plainer...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Indeed, the vast majority will never get to leave their names in the history annals, but they're not the empty space between the lines. They're the pages themselves.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I'm sorry, I talked your ear off there...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Sir, your handwriting is really beautiful.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Oh, well, this... it's my only skill, really. I can still remember when the High Minister gave me this transcriber job.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I can never write my name properly. Grandfather's gotten on my case about it more times than I can remember.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Handwriting is a long road. Just keep at it, and you'll see change eventually.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Maybe you could be my calligraphy teacher, then?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I would never pose as your teacher with my modest brushwork, Miss. But...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Right... I have two copybooks here. I copy from them all the time myself. The forms are very regular—it's perfect for beginners.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: If you don't mind, Miss Ning, you can... you can have these as your birthday present.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: How did you know my birthday's today?

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Well, they decorate the estate so brightly this time every year, you see. I've spent long enough here that I've heard.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Miss Ning... Happy birthday.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Th—Thank you.
That conversation always stayed with me. I liked how he talked, and how he saw things.
And I don't know why—I can't really say—but he felt so close to me, in a way.
But after that, I saw him much less around the estate. The next time I got to talk to him, it was years and years later.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather's cold has lasted for a month by now, and it's still not getting any better. Now it's almost winter—it might only get worse at this rate. We'll be counting on you for the next while, doctor.

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: The High Minister's malady is mostly from overwork. You could remind him to rest more often, my lady...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Mm-hm, I will—

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Ah.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: Sorry! I'm sorry...

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I apologize for running into you, Miss.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... *cough* *hack*—Very... very sorry...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It's—it's alright! Sir... are you okay?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Why don't you sit down and rest for a while? You really look... quite ill.

steps.name: Gu Quan
steps.text: I'm fine... I'm fine.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Sir, you dropped your—sir?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Are these... painkillers?

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: *hiss*... Strong painkillers at that... Whoever that was, he must be quite badly ill.

spans.text: painkillers at that... Whoever that was, he must be quite badly ill.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Doctor, if you're free, could I ask you to attend to that man too? You can bill his medical expenses to me.
I was worried about Grandfather's condition at the time, and didn't pay that encounter much mind—I was just planning to pay him a visit later at some point, when I had the time.
But after that winter, I never saw him again.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Doctor, thank you so much for all your work. Grandfather's back in perfect health now.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Right. And about the man I asked you to attend to...

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: Oh, you mean that Gu Quan man.

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: He died.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Was it his illness...?

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: No... I hear some kind of accident took him while he was on his way to Victoria.

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: But given his health, I can't imagine he'd have lived much longer even then...

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: Truth is, last I met him, his malady had taken root in his vitals—I could hear it in his breathing. I can't imagine how much he was suffering in life...

steps.name: Ning's Physician
steps.text: And it's a mystery to me why he'd decide to travel so far while that sick...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: This... very room. It was the study Sir Gu Quan was using.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: It's been ten years since he passed away. The place has gone through some changes in that time.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: This...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I couldn't tell you why... but I kept hold of this medicine bottle ever since.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Blaze... I really am so sorry...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: He was—my dad was nothing like that...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: I don't think he was ever that fighting fit, but he was never weak. Whenever I was with him, he always had this light in his eyes—

spans.text: I don't think he was ever that fighting fit, but he was never
Whenever I was with him, he always had this light in his eyes—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: How could...

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Even now, I'm not sure I understand Sir Gu Quan... but I know he was a warm, gentle person. I could tell.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I blamed myself over and over, for not being able to do anything more for him...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Why are you bothering to... tell me all this...?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I know you suspect that my grandfather was somehow behind your father's passing. At the point, I can only tell you what I know, but—

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You told me all of this just to try and convince me Ning Shu is INNOCENT?!

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: N—No.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: I just wanted to implore you... please, find out the truth.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Whether for Sir Gu Quan's sake... or for the sake of the truth itself.

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Whatever that truth—even is...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: Are you...

steps.name: Blaze
steps.text: You don't have to tell me twice... I am gonna get to the bottom of this.

spans.text: You don't have to tell me twice... I
gonna get to the bottom of this.

steps.text: What first struck Lin Qingyan about the Judicial Review Office was the solemn hush.
The first time she ever set foot through this courtroom's door, all noise promptly vanished behind her. She remembers Yu Cheng telling her why it was designed so.
Silence begets peace, peace begets thought, thought begets results.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Shouldn't the Judicial Review Office be drowning in work top to bottom? And yet you've got the office all to yourself, Deputy Minister Lin?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Jie Zhen...? What are you here for?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Censorate routine investigation. There are some issues we'd like to consult you on regarding the Yu Cheng case.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Consultation or investigation, which is it?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Deputy Minister Lin, after working together for years, I implicitly trust you on a personal level.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But the Department of Discipline and Supervision has a lot riding on this case. We have to go through the motions, Lin, if you'll pardon me.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Just... ask what you need to.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Name.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Lin Qingyan.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Gender.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: ...Female.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Um... let's skip the basic info for now. For the next few questions, you don't need to elaborate on your answers, just respond 'yes' or 'no'.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Are you grilling me?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Everything you say from hereon will be recorded. I'm worried what you say could fly against you.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: If you have no further questions, let's begin.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Deputy Minister Lin, you passed Tianshi Bureau assessments in childhood and were exceptionally admitted per your outstanding grades, and followed the esteemed Cyanstorm Count in learning your Lei Fa.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: After graduating from the Tianshi Bureaus, you chose to join the Judicial Review Office, and soon accompanied then-Deputy Minister Yu Cheng in investigations all across the realm.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: In just a year, from Registrar, you rose several ranks to become the youngest Deputy Minister in the history of Yan.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Is this background, as stated, true?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: In your third month with the Judicial Review Office, as Registrar, you handed in a whistleblower report to Discipline and Supervision. It accused the Right Assistant Revenue Minister of embezzlement and extortion, and you recovered ten million in stolen assets.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: In your fifth month, in Changji, you essentially singlehandedly shone light on the local academy's examination fraud. Over a hundred mandarins were implicated in this, the highest of which was second-rank, all were eventually rounded up.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Upon becoming Deputy Minister, you handled the case of former Judicial Review Office Deputy Minister Yu Cheng forging evidence, causing him to be expelled from the Office's Haoran Pavilion, with all status stripped from him thereafter...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Are these case histories, as stated, true?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: ...Yes.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: With an academic background like this, surely everyone lauds you as a young up-and-comer blessed to the gills with talent.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: And yet people can't help but wonder—what gives such a greenhand mandarin the courage, the capacity to handle these cases?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Can you get to the point?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: If I'm remembering right, your good mother and father were Tianshis at the Chamber of Heaven's Designs, spending years building much in the north, even being vested personally by the True Lung.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: The Lin family's a well-bred one, many Tianshi giants in its line. And on top of that, rumor has it they're quite closely-knit with the Lord Exorcist's household.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: As for Cyanstorm Count... I think even the rank fails to sufficiently capture your shifu's importance to Great Yan.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: ...Are these relationships, as stated, true?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Jie Zhen, what are you doing?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: You need only answer 'yes' or 'no', Deputy Minister Lin.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Don't think I'm deaf to your connotations... You're trying to say, it was only by leaning on my background that I could take on Judicial cases all these years?!

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: ...I certainly didn't say that at any point.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Having known each other for years, I would never doubt your integrity. The Lin Qingyan in my mind's eye has always been a pursuer of justice.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: But why, Lin, do you not pursue now?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Jie Zhen... Just why did you come to see me today?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: How much do you really know about the Yu Cheng affair?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: As I just said, I'm here to see you today on routine business.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: As for the Yu Cheng case, what I heard in the courtroom that day is all I know.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: What makes you so dead-set on the case, Censor Jie Zhen?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Before you decided you'd investigate it, I remember we actually had an argument.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I'm going to speak out of line here... the whole stripping of his rank aside, I really do respect people like Yu Cheng.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Now of all times, you're going to defend him again?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: If a law enforcer does not themselves abide by the law, that's abuse of power. That goes for every last member of the Three Organs of Justice—what kind of double-standard could you possibly be applying here?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: No, no... The Judicial Review Office's verdict is settled on Yu Cheng's mistake. I've little more to say there.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I'm just very curious... What kind of truth could have pushed him to such means to find it?

spans.text: could have pushed him to such means to find it?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: You must be more familiar with Yu Cheng than me.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: In your opinion, was he a smart man?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Naturally. When it comes to sniffing out lies or chasing down leads, I'm no match for him.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Then did you ever wonder if, supposing Yu Cheng truly intended to cover up his own forgery, you should have been able to make such short work of the case?

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: You're telling me he let me find him out on purpose? What for?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: That, I don't know. But he put you in charge of the scrollery fire case... To an outsider, I don't think I can say that Yu Cheng had no faith in you.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: You've been all over Baizao the past few days investigating that case, I know that. I've heard as much.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: And yet since yesterday, you've been loitering in the Judicial Review Office, acting like you've been grounded.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: I can't help being curious—what made you go and give up on pursuing this case?

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Are you afraid of offending the high and mighty? No, that's not like the Lin Qingyan I know...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Did someone lofty crack down on you? Can't be, I think. You're sitting here in the office, after all, not in a Judicial prison cell.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: If not that, then all my pondering can only produce one answer...

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: You're scared that if you continue, you'll implicate someone you know.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Seems I guessed right.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: In the thick of things, your concern clouds your judgment. It's like you've forgotten the simplest of truths.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Don't miss the forest for the trees.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: If you can't hide it, you may as well tip it out. Show it some sunlight.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: Mr. Censor, you've really served up a lesson for me today.

steps.name: Jie Zhen
steps.text: Not at all. I think the hush of this office must've helped you figure out plenty by yourself.

steps.name: Lin Qingyan
steps.text: I know what I must do.

steps.name: Worried Official
steps.text: Madam, I went to ask Deputy Minister Lin if she wanted anything to eat, since I saw she hadn't left the office all day, but—but she...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: When did she go missing?

steps.name: Worried Official
steps.text: I—I don't know, nobody's seen her at all...
A biting chill gusts through, the stiff breeze curling papers and sending them dancing madly through the air.
A wide-open window clatters against its wall. On the table beneath it, a ceremonial gown lies neatly folded and topped with a document, pressed down in place by an ink stone.
It is Lin Qingyan's written resignation.
Watching as Blaze vanishes far into the distance, Ning Shu clutches the door knocker.
The vague dark point vanishes over the crest of the path, but her stare remains fixed there, lingering for the longest time.

steps.name: Ning Shu
steps.text: What are you spacing out at the door for?

steps.name: Ning Yin
steps.text: Grandfather...
